# W6 fixture: the SLOW-TRICKLE emitter for the LogPusher's quadratic regime.
#
# WHY A NEW FIXTURE. `tick` is 30 lines over 30 s — under a total log-bulk
# outage that is ~15 auto-flush ticks, far too short for a triangular
# request-count curve to be distinguishable from noise. `longrun` is already a
# 1 line/s trickle but is fixed at 300 s and takes no parameters. W6-S2b Arm 1
# needs a low-rate, LONG-LIVED emitter whose rate and duration are both knobs,
# because the arm's whole content is the SHAPE of the curve over an outage
# window the scenario chooses.
#
# WHY THE RATE MATTERS, AND WHY THIS SIDE OF THE 4 KiB THRESHOLD.
# `LogPusher.Write` flushes synchronously when the buffer crosses `flushBytes`
# = 4 KiB (`internal/agent/runner.go:255`), and `StartAutoFlush` flushes every
# `logPusherAutoFlushEvery` = 2 s (`runner.go:211`). A trickle of one ~40-byte
# line per second never reaches 4 KiB between ticks, so EVERY flush is a
# timer flush and each one appends exactly one small pending batch while the
# fault is armed. That is the sparse regime: pending grows by one batch per
# tick, `flushLocked` issues one `AppendLogBulk` per pending batch per tick
# (`runner.go:358-366`), so tick k costs k requests and the cumulative cost is
# triangular. It is also the regime that NEVER drops: the 1 MiB pending cap
# (`runner.go:256`) counts line text only (`pendingSizeBytes`, `:438-446`), so
# at ~20-40 bytes per batch the ceiling is tens of thousands of batches — many
# hours. Do not use this fixture to look for the drop marker; that needs a
# chatty fixture (`logburst`) and is a different arm.
#
# The line payload is self-indexing and carries a nanosecond host timestamp, so
# a lost, duplicated or reordered line is measurable from the line itself
# without joining against anything.
#
# PARAMS
#   lines        total lines to emit (default 600)
#   interval_s   seconds between lines (default 1) — `sleep` in the agent image
#                is BusyBox ash's builtin, which accepts fractional values, so
#                0.5 works if a scenario wants 2 lines/s.
# Defaults give 600 lines over ~600 s = 10 minutes at 1 line/s, the upper end
# of the range W6-S2b Arm 1 asks for. There is no step timeout in this repo's
# defaults that a 10-minute step trips.
apiVersion: unified-cd/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: edge-w6-trickle
spec:
  native: true
  params:
    inputs:
      - name: lines
        type: string
        default: "600"
      - name: interval_s
        type: string
        default: "1"
  agentSelector:
    - kind:linux
  steps:
    - name: trickle
      run: |
        echo "trickle-begin lines={{ .Params.lines }} interval_s={{ .Params.interval_s }} $(date -u +%FT%T.%NZ)"
        i=1
        while [ "$i" -le {{ .Params.lines }} ]; do
          echo "trickle $i $(date -u +%FT%T.%NZ)"
          i=$((i + 1))
          sleep {{ .Params.interval_s }}
        done
        echo "trickle-end $(date -u +%FT%T.%NZ)"
